The authors used the hyperbolic (modified) phase-field-crystal (MPFC) model, which accounts for relaxation of both the atomic density field and the atomic flux.
The authors simulated the growth of the (100), (110), and (111) faces of a body-centered cubic (BCC) crystal lattice.
The authors obtained the following sequence of growth velocities: V(100) = 0.519, V(111) = 0.4623, V(110) = 0.4027.
The growth velocity anisotropy V(100)/V(110) was around 1.29 at low driving forces and decreased to around 1.06 at intermediate driving forces.
The anisotropy of the growth velocities also decreased with increasing relaxation time τ.

At high driving forces and relaxation times, the authors observed the formation of disordered crystal structures due to a mismatch between the selected lattice parameter and the equilibrium lattice spacing.
The authors found that the observed sequence of growth velocities agrees with the Bravais law, which states that the faster growth occurs for faces with lower reticular atomic densities.
The reticular atomic densities for the BCC lattice faces are: ρ(100) = a^2, ρ(111) = 27a^2, ρ(110) = a^2, where a is the lattice parameter.
The authors used a computational domain of 27x27x300 dimensionless units with up to 230 grid points and periodic boundary conditions.
The front velocity scale V0 was calculated using the Boltzmann constant kB, temperature T, one-particle number density ρ*, and mobility M.
The authors compared their results to previous studies on the parabolic PFC model, which showed a decreasing front velocity with increasing relaxation time τ.
The authors noted that the contribution of the flux term in the MPFC equation is isotropic and influences each crystal face identically.
The authors suggest that quantitative estimation of the disordered zone around the solidification front is a perspective topic for future study.
